Title: Runaway and Homeless Youth Regions 6 & 7
Description: The purpose of this document is to provide interested parties with information to enable them to prepare and submit a proposal for Runway and Homeless Youth (RHY) Program. This Request for Grant Proposal (RFP) will clarify the Wisconsin Department of Children and Families (DCF) expectations, describe three distinct goals of the RHY Program, and highlight the importance of grounding youth-driven programming in local and regional partnerships, evidence-based/evidence-informed strategies, and data-driven decision-making. The target population for the RHY Program is youth and young adults ages 12-21 who have run away, are at-risk of running away, are homeless, or are at imminent risk of becoming homeless. Proposers may select a subset of this age range and youth may or may not have a history of child welfare or youth justice involvement. Services must be provided in one of the seven Youth Services Regions, see Appendix 1, Youth Services Regions Map. It is not necessary for the agency to serve the entire region. The State, as represented by DCF, intends to use the results of this RFP to award one (1) RHY Program contract in Youth Services Regions 6 and 7 identified in Appendix 1. Non-profit organizations, local units of government and tribal governments are eligible to apply. Questions should be submitted as described in the RFP Document section 1.8.  Do not submit questions through eSupplier.

Title: Long Term Management of ILF Wetland Mitigation Sites
Description: The purpose of this RFB is to select a contractor to provide Long-Term Management (LTM) services at Wisconsin In-Lieu Fee (ILF) Wetland Mitigation sites. The overall goal of this LTM work is to maintain and improve ILF mitigation sites that have met final performance standards and have been released from performance monitoring. To maintain these sites at current conditions, work will primarily center on annual invasive species control, mowings, and occasional but recurring prescribed burning. The Wisconsin Wetland Conservation Trust (WWCT) is Wisconsin’s ILF wetland mitigation program. To date, the WWCT has restored 14 sites totaling 850 acres. ILF mitigation sites must meet vegetative performance standards, typically for five years. After the final performance standards has been met (at least 80% relative cover by native noninvasive species across the entire site), the site will enter the ‘long-term management’ (LTM) phase. During this LTM phase, the sites will be managed, usually annually, to maintain native species cover and wetland function. Typical LTM tasks will consist of invasive species control through herbicide treatments and mowing, prescribed burning, and potentially occasional reseeding. The WWCT created a nonwasting endowment with the Natural Resources Foundation of Wisconsin to provide funding for LTM activities. Once a site is in the LTM phase, it stays in the LTM phase in perpetuity.

Facilitation The consultant will be required to provide professional consulting services to assist in defining the scope and reach of the District’s next three year strategic plan through group facilitation and consensus-building. The District desires an inclusive process involving input from District staff. The professional consultant for the Strategic Plan would be expected to attend and facilitate the staff strategic planning meetings and provide guidance around best practices regarding strategic planning. The consultant will deliver advice and guidance around the process to identify the District’s core values, priorities, goals and outcome measures. The consultant, with staff involvement, will identify the role and goals for the District’s future with respect to major initiatives and opportunities. The consultant will also develop tools to evaluate progress toward achieving the project goals. 2. Draft Strategic Plan and Performance Management System The consultant will complete a draft strategic plan using the planning process referenced in the RFP. The draft Strategic Plan should incorporate elements of the Effective Utility Management Primer and the U.S. Water Alliance’s “An Equitable Water Future” whitepaper. The consultant will obtain input and comment from management staff to ensure appropriate reflection of all interests associated with the successful implementation of the Plan. Performance measures must also be a feature of the Plan to enable progress to be regularly reviewed.

Description:
Notice of Advertisement for Consultant Services Within Bureau of Aeronautics
The Wisconsin Department of Transportation, Bureau of Aeronautics, is accepting letters of interest from qualified firms to provide assistance to BOA.
Project Purpose and Need
The BOA requires the assistance of an aviation consulting firm to conduct a comprehensive statewide study on the integration of Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) into the Wisconsin Aviation System.
Project Description
The Wisconsin Department of Transportation, Bureau of Aeronautics, is seeking consultant services to conduct a comprehensive statewide Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) Study. The study will evaluate how emerging aviation technologies can safely, efficiently, and sustainably support Wisconsin's transportation system while providing practical benefits to communities across the state. Unlike studies focused on major metropolitan areas, this effort emphasizes practical applications that provide statewide connectivity and improved access to essential services.
Scope of Services
Evaluate the current state of the Advanced Air Mobility industry, regulatory environment, and technology readiness.
Assess Wisconsin's existing aviation infrastructure and identify opportunities to support future AAM operations.
Develop policy recommendations for WisDOT, airport sponsors, and local governments.
Develop airport infrastructure recommendations, including facilities, utilities, landside access, charging/fueling, and airspace considerations.
Identify and evaluate up to 10 Wisconsin airports that could serve as early adopters of AAM.
Identify rural-focused use cases with measurable public benefit.
Engage stakeholders across Wisconsin.
Develop phased implementation strategies and an actionable roadmap.
Identify funding opportunities and partnerships.
Areas of Particular Interest
Medical transport and healthcare access
Time-critical delivery of medical supplies
Emergency management and disaster response
Agricultural and natural resource applications
General aviation operations
Flight training and workforce development
Workforce and business connectivity
Tourism and recreation
Mobility for underserved rural communities
Deliverables
Existing Conditions Assessment
Stakeholder Engagement Plan
Rural Use Case Assessment
Airport Infrastructure Recommendations
Policy Recommendations
Identification of up to 10 Early-Adopter Airports
Implementation Roadmap
Funding and Partnership Strategy
Final Wisconsin Advanced Air Mobility Strategy
Executive Summary and Presentation Materials
Project Goal
Develop a practical, data-driven roadmap that positions Wisconsin to capitalize on Advanced Air Mobility technologies by strengthening rural connectivity, enhancing general aviation, supporting economic development, improving access to essential services, and preparing a network of airports for future AAM operations.
Consultant Requirements
Advanced Air Mobility Planning Experience
Policy, Regulatory, and Implementation Experience
Airport and Aviation System Planning Experience
Rural and Regional Transportation Planning Experience
Community and Stakeholder Engagement Experience
Special Skills
Aviation Forecasting and Data Analysis
Airport and Infrastructure Planning Expertise
OEM Partnership Experience
A selection board will review the firm’s qualifications and rank them for further consideration based on the criteria below:
Examples of past AAM Study experience
Years of experience for project team
AAM Planning Experience
Familiarity with FAA guidance and of AAM Industry
Brief example of AAM approach for Wisconsin
Interviews may be conducted with the top two to three candidate firms.
Notice Pertaining to DBE Goals: N/A
Only firms having recent similar experience on airport projects are invited to respond.
A firm’s qualifications will be reported on the bureau’s consultant report form, which can be downloaded from the Wisconsin Department of Transportation Internet site at http://wisconsindot.gov/Pages/doing-bus/aeronautics/airports/forms.aspx. Please submit three copies of the consultant report form. Firms that recently submitted a consultant report form for other projects will not have to file a new form unless they wish to amend a previously filed one.
It is required that a submittal be sent to the bureau stating a firm’s desire to be considered for the above work. This submittal should include the following:
Firms understanding of the project

List of similar work experience
Resume of proposed key personnel
Examples of past AAM Study experience
Years of experience for project team
AAM Planning Experience
Familiarity with FAA guidance and of AAM Industry

Submittals are limited to 20 pages.

The study will evaluate how emerging aviation technologies can safely, efficiently, and sustainably support Wisconsin's transportation system while providing practical benefits to communities across the state. Unlike studies focused on major metropolitan areas, this effort emphasizes practical applications that provide statewide connectivity and improved access to essential services.
Scope of Services
Evaluate the current state of the Advanced Air Mobility industry, regulatory environment, and technology readiness.
Assess Wisconsin's existing aviation infrastructure and identify opportunities to support future AAM operations.
Develop policy recommendations for WisDOT, airport sponsors, and local governments.
Develop airport infrastructure recommendations, including facilities, utilities, landside access, charging/fueling, and airspace considerations.
Identify and evaluate up to 10 Wisconsin airports that could serve as early adopters of AAM.
Identify rural-focused use cases with measurable public benefit.
Engage stakeholders across Wisconsin.
Develop phased implementation strategies and an actionable roadmap.
Identify funding opportunities and partnerships.
Areas of Particular Interest
Medical transport and healthcare access
Time-critical delivery of medical supplies
Emergency management and disaster response
Agricultural and natural resource applications
General aviation operations
Flight training and workforce development
Workforce and business connectivity
Tourism and recreation
Mobility for underserved rural communities
Deliverables
Existing Conditions Assessment
Stakeholder Engagement Plan
Rural Use Case Assessment
Airport Infrastructure Recommendations
Policy Recommendations
Identification of up to 10 Early-Adopter Airports
Implementation Roadmap
Funding and Partnership Strategy
Final Wisconsin Advanced Air Mobility Strategy
Executive Summary and Presentation Materials
Project Goal
Develop a practical, data-driven roadmap that positions Wisconsin to capitalize on Advanced Air Mobility technologies by strengthening rural connectivity, enhancing general aviation, supporting economic development, improving access to essential services, and preparing a network of airports for future AAM operations.
Consultant Requirements
Advanced Air Mobility Planning Experience
Policy, Regulatory, and Implementation Experience
Airport and Aviation System Planning Experience
Rural and Regional Transportation Planning Experience
Community and Stakeholder Engagement Experience
Special Skills
Aviation Forecasting and Data Analysis
Airport and Infrastructure Planning Expertise
OEM Partnership Experience

Examples of past AAM Study experience

Title: Private Property Inflow and Infiltration Reduction - Residential Plumbing Contractors (Pipe Check Program)
Type: Request for Qualifications (RFQ ) / Request for Information (RFI)
Description: The Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District (District) invites residential plumbing contractors who have appropriate experience and performance record to submit qualifications to become an Approved Contractor for the District’s Pipe Check Program. If you are a contractor currently on the list of Pipe Check Approved Contractors, you do not need to apply unless the term of your Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the District expires on or before December 31st, 2026. The purpose of this Request for Qualifications (RFQ) is to prequalify plumbing contractors to perform infiltration and inflow reduction work on residential properties throughout the District’s service area for the Pipe Check Program. Such work, initiated and contracted for by residential property owners, will be partially funded by the District in accordance with the Statement of Policy Infiltration and Inflow (PPII) Reduction Program. An Approved Contractor will remain active on the list of approved contractors for a period of five years, provided a contractor remains in good standing within the program. The list may also be used by the District for other similar projects that may arise. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS ONLY and no guarantee of work. Contractors that wish to be considered for approval must submit a completed application to the District no later than the closing time of 10:00 a.m. Central Time on October 13th, 2026. Applications submitted to the District after this closing date will not be considered at this time. Complete information related to this RFQ is available on the District’s Euna (Bonfire) Procurement Portal website at https://mmsd.bonfirehub.com, Reference # P-3368. All questions related to this RFQ must be directed in writing to Nathan Churchill, District’s Senior Procurement Specialist, at nchurchill@mmsd.com.
